title: How To Get Growth In 2027

How To Get Growth In 2027

Wei He

Gavekal Dragonomics | 28 Oct 2026

China’s growth target for 2026 is now essentially in the bag, despite a series of shocks and surprises, but it is hard for policymakers to be complacent heading into 2027. There is little momentum in domestic demand, with weakness in both consumption and investment, and the sustainability of the current export boom is uncertain. As the organic development of the economy is probably not enough to keep growth going at current rates, there will be more pressure on the government next year to deliver policy support. The central question for 2027 will therefore be how policymakers find ways to boost growth while staying within their many self-imposed strictures. The outcome will not be the hoped-for major stimulus plan that decisively boosts market and household confidence, but the government should still come up with some new measures.The basic framework for macro policy will be set by the annual GDP growth target. That target was lowered from 5% in 2025 to a range of 4.5-5% for 2026, officially because the government wanted to focus more on structural reforms this year (see Governance Over Growth). Consensus forecasts currently expect a further slowdown in 2027, with the IMF calling for just 4.0% GDP growth. But lowering the annual growth target to match those expectations would make it more difficult to achieve other targets for sustained growth over the decade to 2035 (see The Message From More Growth Targets).
